recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

## Arbitrages (font foi)
K1. Disposition paramétrique. `Layout` associe à chaque feuille une plage d'octets `(allocation, offset, size)` d'une allocation MM-02 ; elle ne fixe ni ABI, ni alignement de type, ni ordre des champs. Obligations `LayoutWF` : (a) les feuilles d'un même emplacement racine sont dans la même allocation ; (b) deux feuilles distinctes ont des plages disjointes ; (c) chaque plage est incluse dans son allocation ; (d) une forme à une feuille peut avoir une taille nulle. Aucune autre hypothèse.
K2. Racines et allocations.
  - Racine locale d'un cadre ou statique ↔ allocation automatique ou statique ; son autorité de désallocation est un jeton propre au cadre, compatible par construction.
  - Racine créée par `alloc` ↔ allocation créée par `AllocStep`.
  - Partie ↔ sous-plage de l'allocation de sa racine ; bloc d'arène ↔ sous-plage de l'allocation du stockage de l'arène, sans allocation propre.
  - Le choix de la base d'une nouvelle allocation est un paramètre `Placement`, dont l'obligation est `AllocPre` de MM-02 (fraîcheur, alignement, non-chevauchement des allocations vivantes) ; `K.Satisfiable` implique l'existence d'un placement valide.
K3. Relation de représentation `Repr k L s3 s2` : `LayoutWF` ; toute racine utilisable a son allocation vivante ; toute feuille `Init` a tous ses octets initialisés dans MM-02 ; une racine morte par `free` ou par sortie de cadre a son allocation morte ; une racine morte par `endUse` (stockage possédé non libéré) garde son allocation vivante. État initial : `Repr` entre `S3.init statics` et l'état MM-02 obtenu depuis `State.empty` par les `AllocStep` des statiques, puis l'écriture des statiques déclarées `Init`.
K4. Correspondance des pas, périmètre de la passe 1 :
  - `read3` ↦ `ReadStep` sur chaque plage lue, accès de provenance = allocation de la racine, autorité `read` ;
  - `write3`, `writeShared` ↦ `WriteStep`, autorité `write` ;
  - `alloc` `ok` ↦ `AllocStep` ; `alloc` `fail` ↦ aucun pas ;
  - `free` ↦ `DeallocStep`, autorité `Compatible` issue de `FreeCompat` ;
  - `enterFrame` ↦ un `AllocStep` par racine locale ; `exitFrame` ↦ un `DeallocStep` par allocation automatique du cadre, et aucun pour le stockage possédé qui meurt avec lui (fuite si non libéré) ;
  - `derive`, `split`, `release`, `depend`, `endUse`, `pin`, `unpin`, `newArena`, `reset` ↦ aucun pas.
  `transfer`, `store` et `issue` sont hors de cette passe.
K5. Obligations opaques de MM-02 : `stat` (concurrence) est vrai dans le fragment séquentiel ; `dec` (alignement d'accès, validité de représentation) est une hypothèse paramétrique explicite, jamais instanciée par `True` sans le signaler.

## Étapes (un commit par étape)
1. K1–K3 : `Layout`, `LayoutWF`, `Placement`, `Repr`, `repr_init`.
2. R1 : `read3` `ok` et `Repr` ⇒ `ReadStep` `ok` sur chaque plage, jamais `ub`, et la valeur lue est celle des octets. R2 : `write3`, `writeShared` `ok` et `Repr` ⇒ `WriteStep` `ok`, et `Repr` préservée.
3. R6 (périmètre K4) : pour chaque opération, `ok` en MM-03 et `Repr` ⇒ la séquence MM-02 associée n'a que des issues `ok`, et les états d'arrivée sont en `Repr` ; `alloc` `fail` ⇒ aucun pas, `Repr` préservée.
4. R4 : sur un état en `Repr` avec un état atteint de MM-03, aucune autorité active ne couvre une feuille dont l'allocation MM-02 est morte (depuis `NoDangling`).
5. `exclusive_bytes` : sous `Repr` et I1, si une autorité a le mode effectif `Modify` sur une feuille, aucune autre autorité active qui n'en descend pas n'a de mode effectif sur une feuille dont la plage chevauche la sienne. Justification mémoire du non-aliasing, côté noyau seulement.
6. Cas : un témoin par opération du périmètre, depuis `S3.init`, avec l'état MM-02 en `Repr` et la séquence MM-02 exhibée.

import Ern.MM02
import Ern.MM03

/-!
# Refinement MM-03.3 v0.3 → MM-02 v0.4 (milestone 2, pass 1)

Representation of the abstract states of MM-03.3 (module `Ern.MM03`) by the states of the abstract
machine of MM-02 (module `Ern.MM02`), and refinement of the operations in the scope of the
arbitrage K4 of the task. Both modules are imported unchanged; a lemma they lack is proved here.

The arbitrages K1–K5 of the task are cited as `K1`…`K5`. The rules of the specifications are cited
as `MM-02.x` (MM-02 v0.4) and `MM-03.3 …` (MM-03.3 v0.3 révisée). Out of scope: `transfer`,
`store`, `issue`, concurrency, real `DDSound`, stability of pinned addresses, low-level translation.
The decisions not dictated by the texts are listed in the report `formal/reports/MM23_v0.1.md`,
section (c); the gaps between the drafts and their texts, section (f).
-/

namespace Ern.MM23

open Ern.MM03

/-! ## Allocations of the MM-02 state -/

/-- The MM-02 allocation `i` is registered (MM-02.2) and satisfies `p`. -/
def AllocP (s2 : MM02.State) (i : Nat) (p : MM02.Alloc → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ a, s2.allocs i = some a ∧ p a

instance (s2 : MM02.State) (i : Nat) (p : MM02.Alloc → Prop) [DecidablePred p] :
    Decidable (AllocP s2 i p) :=
  match h : s2.allocs i with
  | some a =>
    if ha : p a then isTrue ⟨a, h, ha⟩
    else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hb'⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb; exact ha hb'
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb

/-- The MM-02 allocation `i` is registered and live (MM-02.2). -/
abbrev LiveAlloc (s2 : MM02.State) (i : Nat) : Prop := AllocP s2 i (·.live = true)

/-- The MM-02 allocation `i` is registered and dead (MM-02.2, MM-02.D). -/
abbrev DeadAlloc (s2 : MM02.State) (i : Nat) : Prop := AllocP s2 i (·.live = false)

/-! ## Layout (K1) -/

/-- K1: layout of the leaves. The leaf `l` occupies the byte range `L l` of an MM-02 allocation:
its identity `alloc`, an offset `off` and a size `len` (an MM-02.4 place). The layout fixes no
ABI, no type alignment and no order of fields. It is a parameter of an execution, defined on
every index, present or future. -/
abbrev Layout := Nat → MM02.Place

/-- K1, obligations `LayoutWF` of a layout in an MM-03 state `s3` and an MM-02 state `s2`:
(a) the leaves of one root place are in one allocation; (b) two distinct leaves in one allocation
have disjoint ranges (`RangeDisjoint`, MM-02.2); (c) the range of every leaf lies within its
allocation, which is registered (MM-02.B, spatial containment). (d) No size is bounded below: a
range may be empty, so a shape of one leaf may have size zero. No other hypothesis. -/
structure LayoutWF (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (s2 : MM02.State) : Prop where
  sameAlloc : ∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
    ∀ l' ∈ footprint s3.P r, (L l).alloc = (L l').alloc
  disjoint : ∀ l < s3.P.length, ∀ l' < s3.P.length, isLeaf s3.P l → isLeaf s3.P l' → l ≠ l' →
    (L l).alloc = (L l').alloc → MM02.RangeDisjoint (L l).off (L l).len (L l').off (L l').len
  within : ∀ l < s3.P.length, isLeaf s3.P l →
    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size

set_option synthInstance.maxSize 512 in
instance (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (s2 : MM02.State) : Decidable (LayoutWF L s3 s2) :=
  decidable_of_iff
    ((∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
      ∀ l' ∈ footprint s3.P r, (L l).alloc = (L l').alloc) ∧
     (∀ l < s3.P.length, ∀ l' < s3.P.length, isLeaf s3.P l → isLeaf s3.P l' → l ≠ l' →
      (L l).alloc = (L l').alloc → MM02.RangeDisjoint (L l).off (L l).len (L l').off (L l').len) ∧
     (∀ l < s3.P.length, isLeaf s3.P l →
      AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩⟩

/-! ## Representation relation (K2, K3) -/

/-- K3: the owner `h` of a root is a frame that is no longer on the stack `F`: the root died by
the exit of its frame. -/
def FrameGone (F : Frames) : Holder → Prop
  | .frame f => f ∉ F
  | .place _ => False

instance (F : Frames) (h : Holder) : Decidable (FrameGone F h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold FrameGone <;> infer_instance

/-- K2: deallocation token of the allocation of a root owned by `h`: the token `tok f` proper to
the frame `f` when `h` is the frame `f`; none is fixed for a root owned by a place. -/
def tokOf (tok : Nat → Nat) : Holder → Option Nat
  | .frame f => some (tok f)
  | .place _ => none

/-- K3, the decidable part of the relation of representation between an MM-03 state `s3` and an
MM-02 state `s2`, for the layout `L`, the frame tokens `tok`, the provider tokens `ptok` and the
ghost `provOf` (L4: a root allocated by `alloc` ↦ its provider):
- `lwf`: `LayoutWF` (K1);
- `inj`: two distinct root places are in distinct allocations (K2: a root corresponds to an
  allocation; a part to a sub-range of the allocation of its root, by `LayoutWF.sameAlloc`);
- `tokens`: the allocation of a root owned by the frame `f` has the token `tok f` (K2);
- `provTokens`: the allocation of a root allocated from the provider `pr` has the token `ptok pr`
  (L4);
- `live`: every usable root has its allocation live (K3);
- `init`: every `Init` leaf has all its bytes initialised (K3; L3: a `Moved` or `Uninit` leaf
  imposes nothing);
- `freed`: a root dead by `free` has its allocation dead (K3);
- `exited`: a root dead by the exit of its frame has its allocation dead (K3);
- `leaked`: a root owned by a place, not usable and not freed keeps its allocation live (K3 for a
  root dead by `endUse`; L5 for owned storage that dies with a freed root or with its frame).
It does not read the contracts `K` (L3). -/
structure ReprB (tok ptok : Nat → Nat) (provOf : Nat → Option Nat) (L : Layout) (s3 : S3)
    (s2 : MM02.State) : Prop where
  lwf : LayoutWF L s3 s2
  inj : ∀ r < s3.P.length, ∀ r' < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → RootPlace s3.P r' → r ≠ r' →
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r, ∀ l' ∈ footprint s3.P r', (L l).alloc ≠ (L l').alloc
  tokens : ∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → OptP (s3.P[r]?) (fun pl =>
    OptP (tokOf tok pl.owner) (fun d => ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
      AllocP s2 (L l).alloc (·.freeAuth = some d)) True) True
  provTokens : ∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → OptP (provOf r) (fun pr =>
    ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r, AllocP s2 (L l).alloc (·.freeAuth = some (ptok pr))) True
  live : ∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → s3.Usable r → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
    LiveAlloc s2 (L l).alloc
  init : ∀ l < s3.P.length, isLeaf s3.P l → s3.I l = .init →
    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len
  freed : ∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → s3.freed r = true → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
    DeadAlloc s2 (L l).alloc
  exited : ∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → OptP (s3.P[r]?) (fun pl => FrameGone s3.F pl.owner)
    False → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r, DeadAlloc s2 (L l).alloc
  leaked : ∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → ¬ s3.Usable r → s3.freed r = false →
    OptP (s3.P[r]?) (fun pl => pl.owner.isPlace = true) False → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
    LiveAlloc s2 (L l).alloc

set_option synthInstance.maxSize 8192 in
instance (tok ptok : Nat → Nat) (provOf : Nat → Option Nat) (L : Layout) (s3 : S3)
    (s2 : MM02.State) : Decidable (ReprB tok ptok provOf L s3 s2) :=
  decidable_of_iff
    (LayoutWF L s3 s2 ∧
     (∀ r < s3.P.length, ∀ r' < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → RootPlace s3.P r' → r ≠ r' →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r, ∀ l' ∈ footprint s3.P r', (L l).alloc ≠ (L l').alloc) ∧
     (∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → OptP (s3.P[r]?) (fun pl =>
      OptP (tokOf tok pl.owner) (fun d => ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
        AllocP s2 (L l).alloc (·.freeAuth = some d)) True) True) ∧
     (∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → OptP (provOf r) (fun pr =>
      ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r, AllocP s2 (L l).alloc (·.freeAuth = some (ptok pr))) True) ∧
     (∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → s3.Usable r → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
      LiveAlloc s2 (L l).alloc) ∧
     (∀ l < s3.P.length, isLeaf s3.P l → s3.I l = .init →
      AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len) ∧
     (∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → s3.freed r = true → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
      DeadAlloc s2 (L l).alloc) ∧
     (∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r →
      OptP (s3.P[r]?) (fun pl => FrameGone s3.F pl.owner) False → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
      DeadAlloc s2 (L l).alloc) ∧
     (∀ r < s3.P.length, RootPlace s3.P r → ¬ s3.Usable r → s3.freed r = false →
      OptP (s3.P[r]?) (fun pl => pl.owner.isPlace = true) False → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
      LiveAlloc s2 (L l).alloc))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, c', d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, c', d, e, f, g, h⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, c', d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, c', d, e, f, g, h⟩⟩

/-- K3, L3: relation of representation `Repr`: `ReprB`, and the MM-02 state has fresh identities
(`MM02.WF`, MM-02.A). Not decidable (`WF` quantifies over every identity); `ReprB` is. -/
structure Repr (tok ptok : Nat → Nat) (provOf : Nat → Option Nat) (L : Layout) (s3 : S3)
    (s2 : MM02.State) : Prop extends ReprB tok ptok provOf L s3 s2 where
  wf2 : MM02.WF s2

/-! ## Sequences of MM-02 operations (MM-02.H, K4, K5) -/

/-- An MM-02 operation with its arguments (MM-02.H): read, write, deallocation, allocation. -/
inductive Op2 where
  | read (ac : MM02.Access)
  | write (ac : MM02.Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
  | dealloc (id auth : Nat)
  | alloc (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat)

/-- Effect of an operation of outcome `ok` (MM-02.H.2): a read leaves the state unchanged. -/
def Op2.eff : Op2 → MM02.State → MM02.State
  | .read _, s => s
  | .write ac w, s => s.write ac w
  | .dealloc id _, s => s.dealloc id
  | .alloc sp b sz al fa, s => s.alloc sp b sz al fa

/-- State reached by a sequence of operations of outcome `ok`. -/
def exec : MM02.State → List Op2 → MM02.State
  | s, [] => s
  | s, o :: os => exec (o.eff s) os

/-- `p s o` holds for each operation `o` of the sequence, in the state `s` where it runs. -/
def Along (p : MM02.State → Op2 → Prop) : MM02.State → List Op2 → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | s, o :: os => p s o ∧ Along p (o.eff s) os

instance decAlong (p : MM02.State → Op2 → Prop) [h : ∀ s o, Decidable (p s o)] :
    (s : MM02.State) → (os : List Op2) → Decidable (Along p s os)
  | _, [] => isTrue trivial
  | s, o :: os => @instDecidableAnd _ _ (h s o) (decAlong p (o.eff s) os)

/-- The operation `o` has the outcome `ok` in `s` for its relation (MM-02.H.1): `ReadStep`,
`WriteStep`, `DeallocStep` or `AllocStep`. -/
def OpOk (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec) (ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec)
    (s : MM02.State) : Op2 → Prop
  | .read ac => ∃ v, MM02.ReadStep ObR ac s (.ok v)
  | .write ac w => MM02.WriteStep ObW ac w s (.ok (s.write ac w))
  | .dealloc id au => MM02.DeallocStep C id au s (.ok (s.dealloc id))

have hp := corr_partOf hw hd (l + 1) l l' (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hc
    exact ⟨l', rfl,
      mem_footprint.2 ⟨hp.1, kids_nil_iff.1 (List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero h1), hp⟩⟩

/-- Every leaf of the destination of a transfer is the image of a leaf of the source
(MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered isomorphism `SameShape`: all nodes are matched). -/
theorem corr_leaf_back {s : S3} {src dst : Nat} (hsh : SameShape s.P src dst)
    {l' : Nat} (hl' : l' ∈ footprint s.P dst) :
    ∃ l ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l = some l' := by
  obtain ⟨hlt', hleaf', hpart'⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl'
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrs, hc⟩ := hsh.2 l' (List.mem_range.2 hlt') hpart'
  have h1 := hsh.1 r hr hrs
  rw [hc] at h1
  have h1 : (kids s.P l').length = (kids s.P r).length := h1
  rw [kids_nil_iff.2 hleaf'] at h1
  exact ⟨r, mem_footprint.2 ⟨List.mem_range.1 hr,
    kids_nil_iff.1 (List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero h1.symm), hrs⟩, hc⟩

/-- `corr` is injective on the parts of the source of a transfer (MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered
isomorphism: the `i`-th child corresponds to the `i`-th child). -/
theorem corr_inj {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hd : dst < s.P.length)
    {r₁ r₂ x : Nat} (h₁ : partOf s.P r₁ src) (h₂ : partOf s.P r₂ src)
    (e₁ : corr s.P src dst r₁ = some x) (e₂ : corr s.P src dst r₂ = some x) : r₁ = r₂ :=
  corr_inj_aux hw hd (r₁ + r₂ + 1) r₁ r₂ x (Nat.lt_succ_self _) h₁ h₂ e₁ e₂

/-! ## R6 (MM-03.3 §9.2; K4) -/

/-- MM-03.3.8 (`Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`) and K4 ("`free` ↦ `DeallocStep`, autorité
`Compatible` issue de `FreeCompat`"): obligation of the contracts towards MM-02 for `free p auth` in
the state `s2`: when the contracts permit it, every leaf of `p` is in an allocation with a token
compatible with `auth` (MM-02.D). -/
def FreeSound (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (s2 : MM02.State)
    (p auth : Nat) : Prop :=
  k.Deallocable p → k.FreeCompat p auth → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P p,
    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => ∃ d, a.freeAuth = some d ∧ C auth d

/-- K2: the token proper to each frame is compatible with itself (MM-02.D): the authority that
`exitFrame` presents for an automatic allocation of the frame `f` is `tok f`, compatible by
construction. -/
def TokCompat (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (tok : Nat → Nat) : Prop := ∀ f, C (tok f) (tok f)

theorem exec_readOps (s2 s2' : MM02.State) (L : Layout) :
    ∀ ls : List Nat, exec s2 (readOps s2' L ls) = s2
  | [] => rfl
  | _ :: ls => exec_readOps s2 s2' L ls

/-- R6 for `read3` (MM-03.3 §9.2; K4): the reads of MM-02 have the outcome `ok` and the arrival
states are in `Repr`; hypotheses of `r1_read3`. -/
theorem r6_read3 {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec}
    {tok ptok : Nat → Nat} {provOf : Nat → Option Nat}
    {L : Layout} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : MM02.State} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat}
    (hwf : WF3 s3) (hnd : NoDangling s3) (hfl : FpLeaves s3) (hR : Repr tok ptok provOf L s3 s2)
    (h : Read3Step a ls s3 (.ok s3')) (hstat : ∀ s ac, ObR.stat s ac)
    (hdec : ∀ l ∈ ls, ObR.dec s2 (leafAcc s2 L .read l)) :
    AllOk C ObR ObW s2 (readOps s2 L ls) ∧ Repr tok ptok provOf L s3' (exec s2 (readOps s2 L ls)) := by
  have h1 := r1_read3 hwf hnd hfl hR h hstat hdec
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  refine ⟨?_, by rw [exec_readOps]; exact hR⟩
  have : ∀ ls', (∀ l ∈ ls', l ∈ ls) → AllOk C ObR ObW s2 (readOps s2 L ls') := fun ls' => by
    induction ls' with
    | nil => exact fun _ => trivial
    | cons l ls' ih =>
      intro hs
      obtain ⟨al, -, -, hok, -⟩ := h1 l (hs l (List.mem_cons_self ..))
      exact ⟨⟨_, hok⟩, ih fun l' hl' => hs l' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl')⟩
  exact this ls fun _ h => h

/-- R6 for `alloc` of outcome `ok` (MM-03.3 §9.2, O14; K4: `alloc` `ok` ↦ `AllocStep`; L2: the
shape has one root; L4: the token of the allocation is the token `ptok pr` of the provider, and the
ghost `provOf` maps the new root to `pr`): the allocation of MM-02, at the base chosen by the
placement, has the outcome `ok`, and the arrival states are in `Repr`, for every geometry of valid
alignment and every layout of the new leaves in the fresh allocation (`NewLayout`). -/
theorem r6_alloc {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec}
    {k : K} {tok ptok : Nat → Nat} {provOf : Nat → Option Nat} {L : Layout} {s3 s3' : S3}
    {s2 : MM02.State} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)} {pl : Placement}
    {g : Nat → Geom} {i : Nat} (hwf : WF3 s3) (hR : Repr tok ptok provOf L s3 s2)
    (hpl : PlacementOK pl) (hg : 0 < (g i).align ∧ MM02.Pow2 (g i).align)
    (h : MM03.AllocStep k pr ow ls s3 (.ok s3')) (hone : rootIdx ls = [i])
    (hprov : provOf (s3.P.length + i) = some pr)
    (hNL : NewLayout L s3'.P s3.P.length s2.next g [i]) :
    AllOk C ObR ObW s2 [.alloc (g i).space (pl s2 (g i)) (g i).size (g i).align (some (ptok pr))] ∧
      Repr tok ptok provOf L s3'
        (exec s2 [.alloc (g i).space (pl s2 (g i)) (g i).size (g i).align (some (ptok pr))]) := by
  cases h with
  | ok hst _ =>
    have e : allocOps pl g (some (ptok pr)) s2 [i] =
        [.alloc (g i).space (pl s2 (g i)) (g i).size (g i).align (some (ptok pr))] := rfl
    rw [← e, ← hone]
    refine ⟨allocOps_ok hpl _ _ hR.wf2 (by
        rw [hone]; intro j hj; rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hj]; exact hg),
      repr_extend (hd := .place ow) hR.toReprB hR.wf2 rfl hst.2.2.2.2.2.1
        (fun q hq hu => alloc_usable_back hwf hu hq) (fun _ _ hu => alloc_usable_old hu)
        (fun i hi => alloc_usable_new hst (i + 1) i (Nat.lt_succ_self i) hi) (fun _ => rfl)
        (fun l hl => ?_) (fun _ _ _ _ h => h) (fun _ h => by cases h)
        (fun j hj => by rw [hone, List.mem_singleton] at hj; subst hj; rw [hprov]; rfl)
        (by rw [hone]; exact hNL), exec_wf _ _ hR.wf2⟩
    simp only [allocEff] at hl
    split at hl
    · cases hl
    · rename_i hn
      refine ⟨by omega, ?_⟩
      split at hl
      · exact hst.2.2.2.2.1 l ‹_›
      · exact hl

/-- R6 for `alloc` of outcome `fail` (MM-03.3 §9.2, O14; K4: `alloc` `fail` ↦ no step): the state
is unchanged and stays in `Repr`. -/
theorem r6_alloc_fail {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec}
    {k : K} {tok ptok : Nat → Nat} {provOf : Nat → Option Nat}
    {L : Layout} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : MM02.State} {pr ow : Nat}
    {ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)} (hR : Repr tok ptok provOf L s3 s2)
    (h : MM03.AllocStep k pr ow ls s3 (.fail s3')) :
    AllOk C ObR ObW s2 [] ∧ Repr tok ptok provOf L s3' (exec s2 []) := by
  obtain ⟨rfl, -⟩ := alloc_fail_unchanged h; exact ⟨trivial, hR⟩

/-- L4: `FreeCompat p auth` instantiated by `Compatible auth (ptok (provOf p))`: `p` is a root
allocated from a provider `pr`, and `auth` is compatible with the token of `pr`. -/
def FreeCompatInst (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ptok : Nat → Nat) (provOf : Nat → Option Nat)
    (p auth : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ pr, provOf p = some pr ∧ C auth (ptok pr)

/-- `freeSound_derived` (L4, replaces the hypothesis `FreeSound` of pass 1): under `ReprB`, when
the contracts instantiate `FreeCompat` by `Compatible auth (ptok (provOf p))`, the obligation
`FreeSound` of `free p auth` holds for the root `p`. The content is the clause `provTokens` of
`Repr`: the MM-02 allocation of an allocated root keeps the token of its provider, a clause that
every step preserves (`r6_*`, `simulation`). -/
theorem freeSound_derived {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {tok ptok : Nat → Nat}
    {provOf : Nat → Option Nat} {L : Layout} {s3 : S3} {s2 : MM02.State} {p auth : Nat}
    (hR : ReprB tok ptok provOf L s3 s2) (hp : RootPlace s3.P p)
    (hfc : k.FreeCompat p auth → FreeCompatInst C ptok provOf p auth) :
    FreeSound k C L s3 s2 p auth := by
  intro _ hf l hl
  obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hc⟩ := hfc hf
  have := hR.provTokens p hp.1 hp
  rw [hpr] at this
  exact (this l hl).mono fun _ h => ⟨_, h, hc⟩

/-- R6 for `free` (MM-03.3 §9.2, O13; K4: `free` ↦ `DeallocStep` of the allocation of the root,
authority `auth`; L4: `FreeCompat` instantiated by `Compatible auth (ptok (provOf p))`; L5: one
`DeallocStep`, the storage owned by `p` keeps its allocation live): under `WF3`, the deallocation
has the outcome `ok` and the arrival states are in `Repr`. -/
theorem r6_free {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec}
    {k : K} {tok ptok : Nat → Nat} {provOf : Nat → Option Nat} {L : Layout} {s3 s3' : S3}
    {s2 : MM02.State} {p auth : Nat} (hwf : WF3 s3) (hR : Repr tok ptok provOf L s3 s2)
    (hfc : k.FreeCompat p auth → FreeCompatInst C ptok provOf p auth)
    (h : FreeStep k p auth s3 (.ok s3')) :
    AllOk C ObR ObW s2 (deallocOps [rootAlloc L s3.P p] auth) ∧
      Repr tok ptok provOf L s3' (exec s2 (deallocOps [rootAlloc L s3.P p] auth)) := by
  obtain ⟨⟨hdl, hfc', hu, hor, -⟩, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  have hpr : RootPlace s3.P p := by
    refine ⟨hu.lt, ?_⟩
    unfold OwnedRoot at hor; unfold parentOf
    cases hpl : s3.P[p]? with
    | none => rw [hpl] at hor; exact hor.elim
    | some pl => rw [hpl] at hor; exact hor.1
  have hfs := freeSound_derived (k := k) (C := C) hR.toReprB hpr hfc
  have hl0 := headD_mem_footprint hwf hpr.1
  have hnu : ¬ (freeEff s3 p).Usable p := fun h' => by
    have := h'.dead_false
    simp [freeEff, cleanup, freeS, partOf, hpr.1] at this
  have hne : ∀ r, (freeEff s3 p).Usable r → r ≠ p := fun r h' e => hnu (e ▸ h')
  have hUb : ∀ r, (freeEff s3 p).Usable r → s3.Usable r := fun r h' =>
    S3.Usable.mono (s := s3) (s' := freeEff s3 p) rfl (fun _ h => h) (fun q hq => by
      simp only [freeEff, cleanup, freeS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff] at hq; exact hq.1) h'
  have hdiff : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → r ≠ p → ∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P r,
      (L l).alloc ∉ [rootAlloc L s3.P p] := fun r hr hrp l hl hm => by
    rw [List.mem_singleton] at hm
    exact hR.inj r hr.1 p hpr.1 hr hpr hrp l hl _ hl0 hm
  refine ⟨deallocOps_ok _ _ (List.pairwise_singleton _ _) fun i hi => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hi]
    exact (hR.live p hpr.1 hpr hu _ hl0).and (hfs hdl hfc' _ hl0)
  · refine ⟨?_, exec_wf _ _ hR.wf2⟩
    refine repr_deallocs hR.toReprB _ _ rfl (fun _ h => h) (fun r _ hrt hu' => ⟨hUb r hu',
      hdiff r hrt (hne r hu')⟩) (fun r _ hrt hf => ?_) (fun _ _ _ h => .inl h)
      (fun r _ hrt _ hf _ => ?_)
    · simp only [freeEff, cleanup, freeS, Bool.or_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at hf
      rcases hf with hf | rfl
      · exact .inl hf
      · exact .inr fun l hl => List.mem_singleton.2 (rootAlloc_eq hwf hR.lwf hpr hl)
    · simp only [freeEff, cleanup, freeS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at hf
      exact ⟨.inr hf.1, hdiff r hrt hf.2⟩

/-- R6 for `enterFrame` (MM-03.3 §9.2, O6; K4: `enterFrame` ↦ one `AllocStep` per root local):
under `WF3`, the allocations of the root locals, with the token of the new frame (K2), at the bases
chosen by the placement, have the outcome `ok`, and the arrival states are in `Repr`, for every
geometry of valid alignment and every layout of the new leaves (`NewLayout`); the new roots are not
allocated roots in the ghost `provOf` (L4). The theorem does not need L1: a local owned by a local
is covered too. -/
theorem r6_enter {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec}
    {tok ptok : Nat → Nat} {provOf : Nat → Option Nat}
    {L : Layout} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : MM02.State} {ps : List Nat}
    {ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)} {pl : Placement} {g : Nat → Geom}
    (hwf : WF3 s3) (hR : Repr tok ptok provOf L s3 s2) (hpl : PlacementOK pl)
    (hg : ∀ i ∈ rootIdx ls, 0 < (g i).align ∧ MM02.Pow2 (g i).align)
    (h : EnterStep ps ls s3 (.ok s3'))
    (hprov : ∀ i ∈ rootIdx ls, provOf (s3.P.length + i) = none)
    (hNL : NewLayout L s3'.P s3.P.length s2.next g (rootIdx ls)) :
    AllOk C ObR ObW s2 (allocOps pl g (some (tok s3.nF)) s2 (rootIdx ls)) ∧
      Repr tok ptok provOf L s3' (exec s2 (allocOps pl g (some (tok s3.nF)) s2 (rootIdx ls))) := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  refine ⟨allocOps_ok hpl _ _ hR.wf2 hg, ⟨repr_extend (hd := .frame s3.nF) hR.toReprB hR.wf2 rfl
    (enterPre_shapeOK hpre.1) (fun q hq hu => enter_usable_back hwf hu hq)
    (fun _ _ hu => enter_usable_old hu)
    (fun i hi => enter_usable_new hpre.1 (i + 1) i (Nat.lt_succ_self i) hi) (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun l hl => ?_) (fun q _ pl _ hg => ?_) (fun f e => by cases e; rfl)
    (fun i hi => by rw [hprov i hi]; trivial) hNL, exec_wf _ _ hR.wf2⟩⟩
  · simp only [enterEff] at hl
    split at hl
    · cases hl
    · exact ⟨by omega, hl⟩
  · cases ho : pl.owner with
    | place _ => rw [ho] at hg; exact hg
    | frame f => rw [ho] at hg; exact fun h => hg (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h)

/-- K4 (`exitFrame`): the root places owned by the frame `f`, the roots of its automatic
allocations. -/
def frameRoots (s3 : S3) (f : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range s3.P.length).filter fun r =>
    decide (RootPlace s3.P r) && decide (OptP (s3.P[r]?) (fun pl => pl.owner = .frame f) False)

theorem mem_frameRoots {s3 : S3} {f r : Nat} :
    r ∈ frameRoots s3 f ↔ RootPlace s3.P r ∧ OptP (s3.P[r]?) (fun pl => pl.owner = .frame f) False := by
  simp only [frameRoots, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]
  exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨h.1.1, h.1, h.2⟩⟩

/-- K4 (`exitFrame` ↦ one `DeallocStep` per automatic allocation of the frame, none for the owned
storage that dies with it): the deallocations of the allocations of the root places owned by the
current frame, with its token (K2). A local owned by another local is read as owned storage: no
deallocation (report, (c) 3 and (e) 1; witness `CaseOwnedLocal`). -/
def exitOps (L : Layout) (tok : Nat → Nat) (s3 : S3) : List Op2 :=
  deallocOps ((frameRoots s3 s3.top).map (rootAlloc L s3.P)) (tok s3.top)

/-- R6 for `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §9.2, O7; K4): under `WF3`, `FrameOwnedLive` and the compatibility
of the frame tokens (K2), the deallocations of the automatic allocations of the exited frame have
the outcome `ok`, and the arrival states are in `Repr`: owned storage that dies with the frame
keeps its allocation live (leak). -/
theorem r6_exit {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec}
    {k : K} {tok ptok : Nat → Nat} {provOf : Nat → Option Nat}
    {L : Layout} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : MM02.State} (hwf : WF3 s3)
    (hfo : FrameOwnedLive s3) (hR : Repr tok ptok provOf L s3 s2) (htc : TokCompat C tok)
    (h : ExitStep k s3 (.ok s3')) :

| .writeShared a ls _, s, s' => WriteSharedStep k a ls s (.ok s')
  | .pin p, s, s' => PinStep p s (.ok s')

  | .free p auth, s, s' => FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s')
  | .alloc pr ow ls, s, s' => (∃ i, rootIdx ls = [i]) ∧ AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s')
  | .newArena st i, s, s' => NewArenaStep st i s (.ok s')
  | .issue i via region dst, s, s' => IssueAt k i via region dst s (.ok s')
  | .reset i via, s, s' => ResetAtStep k i via s (.ok s')
  | .store a p, s, s' => StoreStep a p s (.ok s')

/-- A labelled step is a step of `Reachable` (MM-03.3 §10). -/
theorem Step3.step {k : K} {op : Op3} {s s' : S3} (h : Step3 k op s s') : Step k s s' := by
  cases op with
  | derive => exact .kernel (.derive h)
  | split => exact .kernel (.split h)
  | release => exact .kernel (.release h)
  | transfer => exact .kernel (.transfer h)
  | depend => exact .kernel (.depend h)
  | enter => exact .kernel (.enter h.2)
  | exit => exact .kernel (.exit h)
  | read => exact .kernel (.read h)
  | write => exact .kernel (.write h)
  | writeShared => exact .kernel (.writeShared h)
  | pin => exact .kernel (.pin h)
  | unpin => exact .kernel (.unpin h)
  | endUse => exact .kernel (.endUse h)
  | free => exact .kernel (.free h)
  | alloc => exact .kernel (.alloc h.2)
  | newArena => exact .newArena h
  | issue => exact .issue h
  | reset => exact .reset h
  | store => exact .kernel (.store h)

/-- An execution of MM-03 from `S3.init statics` within the envelope of L1 and L2: the operations,
most recent first, and the state reached. -/
inductive Exec3 (k : K) (statics : Statics) : List Op3 → S3 → Prop where
  | init : ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1)) → Exec3 k statics [] (S3.init statics)
  | step {ops : List Op3} {s s' : S3} {op : Op3} : Exec3 k statics ops s → Step3 k op s s' →
      Exec3 k statics (op :: ops) s'

theorem Exec3.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {ops : List Op3} {s : S3}
    (h : Exec3 k statics ops s) : Reachable k statics s := by
  induction h with
  | init hsh => exact .init hsh
  | step _ hs ih => exact Reachable.ofStep ih hs.step

/-- Parameters of the refinement fixed once for a whole execution (step 5): the layout, the frame
and provider tokens (K2, L4), the placement (K2), the geometry of the allocation of each root place,
read on its index, the encoding of pointers (L6), the initial bytes of the statics (K3). -/
structure Params where
  L : Layout
  tok : Nat → Nat
  ptok : Nat → Nat
  pl : Placement
  geom : Nat → Geom
  pe : PtrEnc
  w0 : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat

/-- K4, L6: the MM-02 sequence associated with an MM-03 operation from the states `s3`, `s2`. -/
def assoc (π : Params) : Op3 → S3 → MM02.State → List Op2
  | .read _ ls, _, s2 => readOps s2 π.L ls
  | .write _ ls w, _, s2 => writeOps s2 π.L w ls
  | .writeShared _ ls w, _, s2 => writeOps s2 π.L w ls
  | .transfer src dst, s3, s2 => transferOps s2 π.L s3.P src dst
  | .store a p, s3, s2 => storeOps π.pe s2 π.L s3 a p
  | .issue _ _ region dst, _, s2 => issueOps π.pe s2 π.L region dst
  | .alloc pr _ ls, s3, s2 =>
    allocOps π.pl (fun i => π.geom (s3.P.length + i)) (some (π.ptok pr)) s2 (rootIdx ls)
  | .enter _ ls, s3, s2 =>
    allocOps π.pl (fun i => π.geom (s3.P.length + i)) (some (π.tok s3.nF)) s2 (rootIdx ls)
  | .free p auth, s3, _ => deallocOps [rootAlloc π.L s3.P p] auth
  | .exit, s3, _ => exitOps π.L π.tok s3
  | _, _, _ => []

/-- L4: the ghost `provOf` after an operation: `alloc pr _ ls` maps the places it creates to the
provider `pr`; no other operation changes it. -/
def provStep : Op3 → S3 → (Nat → Option Nat) → Nat → Option Nat
  | .alloc pr _ ls, s3, pv => fun r =>
    if s3.P.length ≤ r ∧ r < s3.P.length + ls.length then some pr else pv r
  | _, _, pv => pv

/-- K3: the MM-02 operations of the initial state with the parameters `π`. -/
def initOpsOf (π : Params) (statics : Statics) : List Op2 :=
  initOps π.pl π.geom π.tok π.L π.w0 statics

/-- The lock-step translation of an MM-03 execution: the operations (most recent first), the MM-03
state, the ghost `provOf`, the MM-02 operations (in the order of execution) and the MM-02 state.
It starts with the MM-02 run of `repr_init`; each MM-03 step appends its associated sequence. It is
determined by the execution and the parameters. -/
inductive Trans (k : K) (statics : Statics) (π : Params) :
    List Op3 → S3 → (Nat → Option Nat) → List Op2 → MM02.State → Prop where
  | init : ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1)) →
      Trans k statics π [] (S3.init statics) (fun _ => none) (initOpsOf π statics)
        (exec MM02.State.empty (initOpsOf π statics))
  | step {ops : List Op3} {s3 s3' : S3} {pv : Nat → Option Nat} {os : List Op2}
      {s2 : MM02.State} {op : Op3} :
      Trans k statics π ops s3 pv os s2 → Step3 k op s3 s3' →
      Trans k statics π (op :: ops) s3' (provStep op s3 pv) (os ++ assoc π op s3 s2)
        (exec s2 (assoc π op s3 s2))

/-- Every MM-03 execution has a translation. -/
theorem Trans.of_exec {k : K} {statics : Statics} (π : Params) {ops : List Op3} {s3 : S3}
    (h : Exec3 k statics ops s3) : ∃ pv os s2, Trans k statics π ops s3 pv os s2 := by
  induction h with
  | init hsh => exact ⟨_, _, _, .init hsh⟩
  | step _ hs ih => obtain ⟨pv, os, s2, ht⟩ := ih; exact ⟨_, _, _, ht.step hs⟩

/-- K1, K2: the layout obligation of an operation that creates root places: the new roots are laid
out in fresh allocations, within their geometry (`NewLayout`). -/
def LayoutObl (π : Params) : Op3 → S3 → S3 → MM02.State → Prop
  | .enter _ ls, s3, s3', s2 =>
    NewLayout π.L s3'.P s3.P.length s2.next (fun i => π.geom (s3.P.length + i)) (rootIdx ls)
  | .alloc _ _ ls, s3, s3', s2 =>
    NewLayout π.L s3'.P s3.P.length s2.next (fun i => π.geom (s3.P.length + i)) (rootIdx ls)
  | _, _, _, _ => True

instance (π : Params) (op : Op3) (s3 s3' : S3) (s2 : MM02.State) :
    Decidable (LayoutObl π op s3 s3' s2) := by
  cases op <;> unfold LayoutObl <;> infer_instance

theorem ReprB.provOf_congr {tok ptok : Nat → Nat} {pv pv' : Nat → Option Nat} {L : Layout}
    {s3 : S3} {s2 : MM02.State} (hR : ReprB tok ptok pv L s3 s2)
    (h : ∀ r < s3.P.length, pv' r = pv r) : ReprB tok ptok pv' L s3 s2 :=
  { hR with provTokens := fun r hr hrt => by rw [h r hr]; exact hR.provTokens r hr hrt }

theorem decAlong_readOps {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec} {s2 s2' : MM02.State}
    {L : Layout} : ∀ {ls : List Nat}, DecAlong ObR ObW s2 (readOps s2' L ls) →
      ∀ l ∈ ls, ObR.dec s2 (leafAcc s2' L .read l)
  | [], _, _, h => by cases h
  | _ :: _, ⟨h0, h⟩, _, hl => by
    rcases List.mem_cons.1 hl with rfl | hl
    · exact h0
    · exact decAlong_readOps h _ hl

/-- L4: the obligation of the contracts at a `free` of the run: `FreeCompat` is instantiated by
the token of the provider recorded by the ghost `provOf` (`FreeCompatInst`). -/
def FreeOblig (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (π : Params) : Op3 → (Nat → Option Nat) → Prop
  | .free p auth, pv => k.FreeCompat p auth → FreeCompatInst C π.ptok pv p auth
  | _, _ => True

/-- The obligations of one step of the run, on the states where it runs: the layout of the new
roots (`LayoutObl`, K1, K2), `dec` along its MM-02 sequence (K5), and `FreeOblig` (L4). -/
def Oblig (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec) (ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec)
    (π : Params) (op : Op3) (s3 s3' : S3) (pv : Nat → Option Nat) (s2 : MM02.State) : Prop :=
  LayoutObl π op s3 s3' s2 ∧ DecAlong ObR ObW s2 (assoc π op s3 s2) ∧ FreeOblig k C π op pv

/-- An execution of MM-03 with its translation (`Trans`) whose every step meets its obligations
(`Oblig`), and whose initial run meets the layout of the statics and `dec`. The obligations bear on
the states of this execution and its run only. -/
inductive SimRun (k : K) (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec)
    (ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec) (statics : Statics) (π : Params) :
    List Op3 → S3 → (Nat → Option Nat) → List Op2 → MM02.State → Prop where
  | init : ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1)) →
      NewLayout π.L (S3.init statics).P 0 0 π.geom (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))) →
      DecAlong ObR ObW MM02.State.empty (initOpsOf π statics) →
      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π [] (S3.init statics) (fun _ => none) (initOpsOf π statics)
        (exec MM02.State.empty (initOpsOf π statics))
  | step {ops : List Op3} {s3 s3' : S3} {pv : Nat → Option Nat} {os : List Op2}
      {s2 : MM02.State} {op : Op3} :
      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π ops s3 pv os s2 → Step3 k op s3 s3' →
      Oblig k C ObR ObW π op s3 s3' pv s2 →
      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π (op :: ops) s3' (provStep op s3 pv) (os ++ assoc π op s3 s2)
        (exec s2 (assoc π op s3 s2))

/-- A `SimRun` is the canonical translation of its execution. -/
theorem SimRun.trans {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec}
    {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec} {statics : Statics} {π : Params} {ops : List Op3} {s3 : S3}
    {pv : Nat → Option Nat} {os : List Op2} {s2 : MM02.State}
    (h : SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π ops s3 pv os s2) : Trans k statics π ops s3 pv os s2 := by
  induction h with
  | init hsh _ _ => exact .init hsh
  | step _ hs _ ih => exact ih.step hs

/-- A `SimRun` is an execution of MM-03. -/
theorem SimRun.exec3 {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec}
    {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec} {statics : Statics} {π : Params} {ops : List Op3} {s3 : S3}
    {pv : Nat → Option Nat} {os : List Op2} {s2 : MM02.State}
    (h : SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π ops s3 pv os s2) : Exec3 k statics ops s3 := by
  induction h with
  | init hsh _ _ => exact .init hsh
  | step _ hs _ ih => exact ih.step hs

/-- `simulation` (step 5): along every execution of MM-03 from `S3.init statics` within the
envelope of L1 and L2, translated with parameters `π` fixed once for the whole execution, whose
steps meet their obligations (`SimRun`), the MM-02 run starts with the run of `repr_init`, appends
at each step the sequence associated by K4 and L6, has only `ok` outcomes, reaches the state `s2`,
and is in `Repr` with the MM-03 state; the MM-03 state is reached, and the ghost `provOf` is empty
beyond the places. Since every prefix of a `SimRun` is a `SimRun`, this holds at each step. The
remaining hypotheses: `DDSound k` (L7: `ddSound_of_layout`); `stat` (K5); the obligation of the
placement and valid alignments (K2); the compatibility of the frame tokens (K2). -/
theorem simulation {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : MM02.ReadOblSpec} {ObW : MM02.WriteOblSpec}
    {k : K} {statics : Statics} {π : Params} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hstatR : ∀ s ac, ObR.stat s ac) (hstatW : ∀ s ac w, ObW.stat s ac w)
    (hpl : PlacementOK π.pl) (hg : ∀ r, 0 < (π.geom r).align ∧ MM02.Pow2 (π.geom r).align)
    (htc : TokCompat C π.tok) :
    ∀ {ops s3 pv os s2}, SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π ops s3 pv os s2 →
      AllOk C ObR ObW MM02.State.empty os ∧ exec MM02.State.empty os = s2 ∧
      Repr π.tok π.ptok pv π.L s3 s2 ∧ Reachable k statics s3 ∧
      ∀ r, s3.P.length ≤ r → pv r = none := by
  intro ops s3 pv os s2 ht

arenas : List Arena
  callParams : Nat → List Nat

/-- Contracts `K` (MM-03.3.8) for an execution. Types are a representation choice: regions as
lists of leaves; `SharedMutable`, `Pinned` and `ExternalDone` on leaves; `Deallocable p` and
`FreeCompat p auth` for `free` (A6); `Satisfiable provider shape s` for `alloc` (B5; C9: it
depends on the current state `s`, with the shape encoded as the locals of `enterFrame`, C6).
`Invalidates` is removed (B9). The obligations of each contract are named hypotheses of theorems, never
fields. -/
structure K where
  DeclaredDisjoint : List Nat → List Nat → Prop
  SharedMutable : Nat → Prop
  Pinned : Nat → Prop
  ExternalDone : Nat → Prop
  Deallocable : Nat → Prop
  FreeCompat : Nat → Nat → Prop
  Satisfiable : Nat → List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) → S3 → Prop

/-- Obligation of `DeclaredDisjoint` (MM-03.3.8): a declaration never covers two regions that
really overlap. -/
def DDSound (k : K) : Prop := ∀ r r', k.DeclaredDisjoint r r' → ∀ l ∈ r, l ∉ r'

/-- `origin` link of the authority with index `i` (MM-03.3.4). -/
def S3.org (s : S3) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (s.A[i]?).bind (·.origin)

/-- Strict ancestors of authority `i` along `origin`: `i` descends from each (MM-03.3.5). -/
def S3.ancs (s : S3) (i : Nat) : List Nat := chain s.org i

/-- Effective anchor of an anchor `x` (C1): the root of its chain of origins (`RootChain`), the
last element of `x :: s.ancs x`. -/
def S3.effAnchor (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Nat := (s.ancs x).getLastD x

/-- Active authority, that is, valid anchor (pass-1 arbitrage 2). -/
def S3.Active (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Prop := ∃ y, s.A[x]? = some y ∧ y.active = true

instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) : Decidable (s.Active x) :=
  match h : s.A[x]? with
  | some y => if hy : y.active = true then isTrue ⟨y, h, hy⟩
    else isFalse fun ⟨y', h', hy'⟩ => by rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact hy hy'
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨_, h', _⟩ => by rw [h] at h'; cases h'

/-- Current frame: the head of the stack (MM-03.3.1). -/
def S3.top (s : S3) : Nat := s.F.headD 0

/-! ## Decidable helpers -/

/-- Predicate on an optional value: `P y` for `some y`, `d` for `none`. -/
def OptP {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) : Prop :=
  match o with
  | some y => P y
  | none => d

instance {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) [DecidablePred P] [Decidable d] :
    Decidable (OptP o P d) :=
  match o with
  | some y => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (P y))
  | none => inferInstanceAs (Decidable d)

theorem lt_of_getElem? {α : Type} {l : List α} {i : Nat} {x : α} (h : l[i]? = some x) :
    i < l.length := (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 h).1

/-! ## Least fixed points on a bounded universe

`Usable` (A5) and `ExercisableAt` (B2) are inductive predicates. Each is the least fixed point of
a monotone rule over identities below a bound `n`; its Kleene iteration is stable after `n + 1`
steps, which makes it decidable. -/

/-- `k`-th Kleene iterate of a rule `R` on Boolean predicates over `Nat`. -/
def kiter (R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool) : Nat → Nat → Bool
  | 0, _ => false
  | k + 1, a => R (kiter R k) a

/-- A monotone rule whose conclusions lie below `n` and which reads its premise only below
`n`. -/
structure KRule (n : Nat) (R : (Nat → Bool) → Nat → Bool) : Prop where
  mono : ∀ p q : Nat → Bool, (∀ a, p a = true → q a = true) → ∀ a, R p a = true → R q a = true
instance (P : List Place) (q : Nat) (h : Holder) : Decidable (heldIn P q h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold heldIn <;> infer_instance

/-- The holder `h` after the transfer of `src` to `dst` (J1): a place, part of `src`, becomes the
corresponding part of `dst` (`corr`, `dst` itself for `src`). Applied to the holders within the
value only. -/
def mvTo (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) : Holder → Holder
  | .place r => .place ((corr P src dst r).getD dst)
  | .frame f => .frame f

/-- Effect of `transfer(source, destination)` (MM-03.3 §3, O4; A4; A5; J1): every leaf of the
destination becomes `Init`, every leaf of the source `Moved`; the anchors of the source, inherited
ones included, join those of the destination and leave the source and its parts; every authority
held by a part of the source (the source included) is now held by the corresponding part of the
destination (A4, J1); every place owned by a part of the source is now owned by the corresponding
part of the destination, without moving, and its root follows (A5, J1, `RootHeld`). -/
def transferEff (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    P := s.P.map fun pl =>
      if heldIn s.P src pl.owner then { pl with owner := mvTo s.P src dst pl.owner } else pl
    I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P dst then .init
      else if l ∈ footprint s.P src then .moved else s.I l
    D := fun q => if q = dst then s.D dst ++ depsOf s src
      else if partOf s.P q src then [] else s.D q
    A := s.A.map fun y =>
      if heldIn s.P src y.holder then { y with holder := mvTo s.P src dst y.holder } else y }

/-- Active derived access covering a leaf of the source and not moved with it
(MM-03.3 §3, O4.4; A4). -/
def ActiveDerivedOutside (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P src y.holder ∧
    ∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P src) False

instance (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Decidable (ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) := by
  unfold ActiveDerivedOutside; infer_instance

/-- Place `q` is owned by `src` or one of its parts, directly or through other owned places,
searched within `k` steps (A5). -/
def ownedWithinF (s : S3) (src : Nat) : Nat → Nat → Bool
  | 0, _ => false
  | k + 1, q =>
    match s.P[q]? with
    | some pl =>
      match pl.owner with
      | .place o => decide (partOf s.P o src) || ownedWithinF s src k o
      | .frame _ => false
    | none => false

/-- Place `q` is owned, transitively, by the value at `src` (A5): its frame changes with the
value when `src` is transferred. -/
def OwnedWithin (s : S3) (src q : Nat) : Prop := ownedWithinF s src (s.P.length + 1) q = true

instance (s : S3) (src q : Nat) : Decidable (OwnedWithin s src q) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ = true))

/-- `OwnedIn P src q` (A5): the owner chain of place `q` reaches a place owned by `src` or one of
its parts. -/
inductive OwnedIn (P : List Place) (src : Nat) : Nat → Prop where
  | direct {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} : P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o → partOf P o src →
      OwnedIn P src q
  | step {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} : P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o → OwnedIn P src o →
      OwnedIn P src q

theorem OwnedIn.lt {P : List Place} {src q : Nat} (h : OwnedIn P src q) : q < P.length := by
  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›

/-- One step of `OwnedIn`, read on a Boolean premise. -/
def owR (s : S3) (src : Nat) (U : Nat → Bool) (q : Nat) : Bool :=
  match s.P[q]? with
  | some pl => match pl.owner with
    | .place o => decide (partOf s.P o src) || (decide (o < s.P.length) && U o)
    | .frame _ => false
  | none => false

Les conditions 4, 5 et 6 ne sont pas définies concrètement par ce noyau ; elles demeurent des obligations explicites et paramétrables. Une écriture brute qui enfreint une obligation de sûreté est un UB ; une interface sûre doit la prévenir ou produire un échec défini.

**Lecture après écriture et non-interférence.** Une écriture valide rend les octets de la plage écrite initialisés. En l’absence d’écriture ou d’invalidation intermédiaire, **toute lecture brute d’octets valide d’une sous-plage incluse dans la plage écrite**, y compris la plage entière, restitue exactement la sous-séquence correspondante du contenu écrit, informations de provenance abstraite comprises, sous réserve des autres conditions de lecture. Une écriture valide ne modifie ni le résultat d’une lecture valide d’une autre allocation ni celui d’une plage disjointe de la plage écrite. Ces propriétés portent sur des octets abstraits et ne préjugent pas de la reconstruction d’une valeur typée.

## MM-02.D — Désallocation

Une désallocation brute réussie exige :

1. une allocation abstraite **vivante** et désallouable ;
2. une **autorité de désallocation compatible** avec celle qu'exige l'allocation.

Cette compatibilité est une relation sémantique ; elle n'exige pas nécessairement l'identité numérique des deux handles d'allocateur, et elle est distincte de la provenance d'accès.

La désallocation réussie termine la validité de l'allocation. Les accès qui portent sa provenance ne peuvent plus lire ou écrire cet ancien stockage. Une tentative de double désallocation par l'opération brute viole une obligation de sûreté et constitue un UB. Une abstraction sûre qui détecte une tentative incompatible avant d'effectuer une opération dangereuse peut produire un échec défini ; cela ne requiert pas une primitive universelle de désallocation vérifiée.

Dans le noyau exploratoire, la compatibilité se définit entre l'autorité présentée et le jeton de désallocation enregistré. Un allocateur de bibliothèque peut imposer, en plus, des contraintes dépendant de son propre état ; elles ne changent pas la signature minimale de la relation de compatibilité du noyau.

**Frontière avec MM-03 :** les droits et accès dépendants d'objets internes à une allocation encore vivante, par exemple après `arena.reset()` ou `stack.rewind(mark)`, doivent également être préservés ou invalidés selon la future discipline d'accès. Il ne s'agit pas d'une troisième précondition vague de MM-02.D, mais d'une obligation à spécifier dans la discipline temporelle.

## MM-02.E — Dérivation restrictive et création d'accès

----
3. Aucun emplacement **encore utilisable après l'effet** ne dépend d'une autorité détenue par `place`, de sa racine, ou d'une autorité qui deviendrait inactive par la mort d'un détenteur possédé.
4. **Aucune feuille dont l’usage se termine, stockage possédé transitivement compris, n’est épinglée**, ni statiquement (`K.Pinned`) ni dynamiquement (`pin`). Une obligation d’épinglage dynamique doit être levée légalement par `unpin` avant ce pas.

**Effet `ok`** : les feuilles de la valeur `place` deviennent `Uninit` ; `place` **reste utilisable comme emplacement** et pourra être réinitialisé légalement. Les autorités détenues par `place` et par les sous-stockages morts sont libérées ; les dépendances de la valeur terminée sont supprimées ; les emplacements possédés transitivement qui cessent de vivre sont marqués morts. L'opération ne déclenche pas automatiquement une désallocation MM-02 : une allocation non libérée peut constituer une fuite, qui n'est pas interdite par cette garantie. **Autre issue :** `reject`.

### O13 — `free(place, auth)`

**Préconditions**

1. `place` est une **racine de stockage possédée par une valeur** (`OwnedRoot`) et non un simple local directement possédé par un cadre ni une partie d'agrégat.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` est établi et `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifie l'autorité de désallocation `auth` ; cet identifiant est opaque au noyau MM-03.
3. Le cadre courant dispose de `Modify` exerçable ; aucune dérivée active sur l'empreinte à libérer n'est détenue en dehors des détenteurs qui meurent ; aucun emplacement survivant n'est ancré sur une autorité de la région libérée ou de ses détenteurs morts.
4. Aucune feuille de l'unité libérée n'est statiquement ou dynamiquement épinglée. La fin d'un usage externe ne transforme pas silencieusement une feuille encore épinglée en unité libérable.

**Effet `ok`** : `place` et le stockage qui cesse de vivre sont marqués morts ; les autorités de ces régions, y compris les racines correspondantes, deviennent inactives, ainsi que celles dont les détenteurs meurent. Les dépendances survivantes doivent rester valides. La correspondance avec une désallocation MM-02 correcte est une obligation du jalon 2, non un axiome de `free`. **Autre issue :** `reject`.

### O14 — `alloc(provider, owner, shape)`

**Préconditions statiques**

1. `shape` est une forme abstraite **non vide**, représentée comme les emplacements locaux d'`enterFrame` ; une allocation de **taille physique zéro** peut être représentée par une forme logique à une feuille.
2. **Toutes les feuilles du fournisseur** sont `Init` ; la mise à jour de ses métadonnées est autorisée par `Modify` exerçable ou par un `writeShared` valide sur des métadonnées `SharedMutable`.
3. Le cadre courant possède `Modify` exerçable sur `owner` ; les nouvelles identités et relations de possession doivent respecter `WF3`, `RootHeld` et les restrictions de vivacité.

**Issues**

- `reject` : une précondition statique ne tient pas ;
- `fail` : les préconditions statiques tiennent, mais `K.Satisfiable(provider,shape,s)` est faux dans l'état considéré ; **aucun changement d'état** ;
- `ok(s')` : création d'une **nouvelle racine** de stockage d'identité fraîche, possédée par `owner` ; ses feuilles commencent `Uninit`, sa nouvelle autorité racine `Modify`, sans origine, est détenue par `owner` ; les métadonnées du fournisseur sont mises à jour seulement conformément à leur droit de modification.

La réussite de l'allocation dépend de l'état du fournisseur : elle ne constitue pas un droit à inventer de la mémoire physique. Le raffinement de cette opération vers `AllocStep` de MM-02 relève du jalon 2.

### O15 — `pin(place)`

Les propriétés de transfert entre threads et de partageabilité ne se déduisent pas du seul présent modèle séquentiel. Elles dépendront des ressources externes, des autorités contenues, des ancres, des restrictions de confinement et du modèle de concurrence de la Spec 2.

## 8. Contrats `K` et obligations de sûreté

Un contrat `K` paramètre des règles de MM-03 sans fabriquer de permissions. Une abstraction sûre utilisant une partie de `K` doit prouver ou satisfaire l'obligation correspondante ; des préconditions ignorées dans une exploration Lean ne constituent pas des garanties du langage.

| Contrat | Obligation externe | Statut pour la formalisation du jalon 1 |
|---|---|---|
| `DeclaredDisjoint` | `DDSound(K)` : aucune région déclarée disjointe de façon fausse alors que des feuilles peuvent se chevaucher | Hypothèse nécessaire à la préservation globale d'I1, notamment pour `split` |
| `Pinned` | I5, interdiction des déplacements physiques incompatibles ; `StaticPinnedBottom` pour les statiques épinglés | Obligation spécialisée ; preuves conditionnées à sa satisfaction |
| `SharedMutable` | Discipline de mutation partagée applicable, avec droits et synchronisations corrects | Le noyau ne prouve ni la stabilité de la valeur observée ni l'absence de data race |
| `ExternalDone` | Le recours externe au stockage est terminé lorsque `unpin` est autorisé | Obligation non vérifiée par le noyau pour les dispositifs externes |
| `Deallocable` | L'emplacement appartient à une unité effectivement libérable | Raccordement à MM-02 au jalon 2 |
| `FreeCompat` | L'autorité opaque de désallocation est compatible avec l'unité libérée | Raccordement à MM-02 au jalon 2 |
| `Satisfiable` | Le fournisseur peut satisfaire la forme demandée **dans l'état courant** | Décide `ok` ou `fail` après validation des préconditions statiques de `alloc` |

`Invalidates` n'est pas un champ de `K` pour le présent noyau : les conditions structurelles de `reset`, de `free` et des dépendances portent directement les obligations d'invalidation pertinentes. La réalisation de `DDSound` à partir de dispositions mémoire réelles fait partie du raffinement de MM-03 vers MM-02.

## 9. Obligations de raffinement vers MM-02

MM-03 définit des emplacements logiques, des autorités, des dépendances et leurs transitions. MM-02 définit les allocations, les octets, les emplacements et les opérations mémoire au niveau concret de son propre modèle. **Le jalon 1 n'est pas une preuve de l'implémentation mémoire concrète** : le jalon 2 doit construire une relation de représentation justifiée entre les deux modèles.

### 9.1 — Correspondances exigées

1. **Emplacements et octets :** associer `P`, les feuilles de `footprint`, leur possession et leurs parties aux unités de stockage, offsets, plages, identités et contraintes d'alignement de MM-02 ; établir une disjonction réelle pour les déclarations `DeclaredDisjoint`.
2. **Autorités et opérations :** rattacher les modes effectifs et `ExercisableAt` aux conditions concrètes de lecture, écriture et validité des pointeurs ; montrer qu'un accès sûr MM-03 satisfait les obligations MM-02, sans confondre possession et représentation binaire.
3. **Initialisation :** relier `Uninit`, `Init` et `Moved` aux valeurs et représentations concrètes ; un `store` d'autorité doit correspondre à l'écriture d'une référence réelle dans **une seule feuille logique** sous une représentation adaptée.
4. **Allocation et désallocation :** relier `alloc` / `free` à `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justifier `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable` et `FreeCompat` ainsi que le cas de taille physique nulle.
5. **Durées de vie :** relier `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, les dépendances et les marques de mort aux effets de validité des stockages réels.
6. **Épinglage et stockage statique :** prouver la compatibilité des déplacements autorisés et des restrictions d'adresses épinglées ; préciser les obligations physiques des statiques et de l'usage externe. La sémantique matérielle spécifique MMIO reste extérieure au noyau séquentiel.
7. **Arènes :** relier les entrées d'arènes, les régions, les émissions, le stockage local/statique/alloué et les métadonnées à des opérations MM-02 ; garantir qu'aucune émission ne réintroduit un accès après invalidation.

| init (val : UInt8) (prov : Option Nat)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- MM-02.2 : allocation abstraite. Son identité est sa clé dans `State.allocs`.
`space` espace d'adressage, `base` adresse de base, `size` étendue, `align` alignement, `live` état
d'existence, `bytes` stockage indexé par décalage depuis `base`,
`freeAuth` jeton de désallocation : si `freeAuth = some d`, les autorités
capables de la désallouer (MM-02.2) sont les `auth` telles que
`Compatible auth d` (MM-02.D) ; `none` si la désallocation n'est pas applicable. -/
structure Alloc where
  space : Nat
  base : Nat
  size : Nat
  align : Nat
  live : Bool
  bytes : Nat → AByte
  freeAuth : Option Nat

/-- MM-02.4 : emplacement, allocation (`alloc`, identité) et portion de son
stockage (`off` décalage, `len` longueur). Interprétation typée et conditions
d'accès non modélisées. -/
  { s with allocs := fun i =>
      if i = ac.prov then (s.allocs i).map (fun a => a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w)
      else s.allocs i }

/-- MM-02.D : désallocation permise de l'allocation `id` avec l'autorité `auth` :
allocation vivante et désallouable (`freeAuth = some d`), autorité compatible
selon la relation paramétrique `Compatible`. -/
def CanDealloc (Compatible : Nat → Nat → Prop) (s : State) (id auth : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ a, s.allocs id = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ ∃ d, a.freeAuth = some d ∧ Compatible auth d

/-- MM-02.D : `CanDealloc` est décidable quand la compatibilité l'est. -/
instance {Compatible : Nat → Nat → Prop} [DecidableRel Compatible] (s : State) (id auth : Nat) :
    Decidable (CanDealloc Compatible s id auth) :=
  match h : s.allocs id with
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb
  | some a =>
    match hf : a.freeAuth with
    | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _, d, hd, _⟩ => by
        rw [h] at hb
        cases hb
        rw [hf] at hd
        cases hd
    | some d =>
      if hc : a.live = true ∧ Compatible auth d then isTrue ⟨a, h, hc.1, d, hf, hc.2⟩
      else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hl, d', hd', hc'⟩ => hc (by
        rw [h] at hb
        cases hb
        rw [hf] at hd'
        cases hd'
        exact ⟨hl, hc'⟩)

/-- MM-02.D : effet d'une désallocation, l'allocation `id` cesse d'exister
(état mort) ; son identité reste consommée (MM-02.A). -/
def State.dealloc (s : State) (id : Nat) : State :=
  { s with allocs := fun i =>
      if i = id then (s.allocs i).map (fun a => { a with live := false }) else s.allocs i }

/-- MM-02.2 et MM-02.A : nouvelle allocation sous l'identité fraîche `s.next`,
vivante ; MM-02.3 : allocation brute nouvellement créée, octets tous `uninit`. -/
def State.alloc (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) : State :=
  { allocs := fun i =>
      if i = s.next then
        some { space, base, size, align, live := true, bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth }
      else s.allocs i
    next := s.next + 1 }

/-- L1: the shape of an `enterFrame` has no owning element: its locals are owned by the frame. -/
def NoOwner (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i < ls.length, (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = none

instance (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Decidable (NoOwner ls) := by
  unfold NoOwner; infer_instance

/-- An `ok` step of MM-03 labelled by its operation, within the envelope of L1 (an `enterFrame`
whose shape has an owning element is outside the language) and L2 (the shape of `alloc` has exactly
one root). -/
def Step3 (k : K) : Op3 → S3 → S3 → Prop
  | .derive src q m, s, s' => DeriveStep src q m s (.ok s')
  | .split src rs, s, s' => SplitStep k src rs s (.ok s')
  | .release a, s, s' => ReleaseStep a s (.ok s')
  | .transfer src dst, s, s' => TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s')
  | .depend q x, s, s' => DependStep q x s (.ok s')
  | .enter ps ls, s, s' => NoOwner ls ∧ EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s')
  | .exit, s, s' => ExitStep k s (.ok s')
  | .read a ls, s, s' => Read3Step a ls s (.ok s')
  | .write a ls _, s, s' => Write3Step a ls s (.ok s')
  | .writeShared a ls _, s, s' => WriteSharedStep k a ls s (.ok s')

/-- Places after `enterFrame`: the locals `ls` appended, owned by the new frame `nF` or by an
earlier local (A5). -/
def enterP (s : S3) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Place :=
  s.P ++ (List.range ls.length).map fun i =>
    ⟨(ls[i]?).bind (·.1), localOwner ls s.nF i, ((ls[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩

/-- Indices, relative to `ls`, of the root locals (no parent). -/
def rootIdx (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Nat :=
  (List.range ls.length).filter fun i => ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)).isNone

/-- Effect of `enterFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O6) with parameters `ps` and locals `ls`: new frame
`nF` pushed; the parameters, held by the caller, are now held by the new frame (A3); locals
appended, uninitialised, without dependency, alive and unpinned; one active root `Modify`
authority per root local on its footprint, held by the owner of the local (pass-1
arbitrage 2; A4); the ghost record `callParams` of the new frame is `ps` (F6). -/
def enterEff (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : S3 :=
  { F := s.nF :: s.F, nF := s.nF + 1, P := enterP s ls
    I := fun l => if s.P.length ≤ l then .uninit else s.I l
    A := mapI (fun j y => if j ∈ ps then { y with holder := .frame s.nF } else y) 0 s.A ++
      (rootIdx ls).map fun i =>
      ⟨.modify, none, footprint (enterP s ls) (s.P.length + i), localOwner ls s.nF i, true⟩
    D := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then [] else s.D q
    dead := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.dead q
    freed := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.freed q
    pin := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.pin q
    arenas := s.arenas
    callParams := fun f => if f = s.nF then ps else s.callParams f }

/-- G1, for one parameter `p` and the state `s'` where the new frame has received its parameters:
if `p` is a `Modify` authority with an origin, that origin, its direct origin only, is
exercisable (A2, B2) at no mode in `s'`. -/
def ParamOriginHidden (s' : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s'.A[p]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify →
    OptP y.origin (fun o => ¬ s'.ExercisableAt o .observe ∧ ¬ s'.ExercisableAt o .modify) True) True

instance (s' : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (ParamOriginHidden s' p) := by
  unfold ParamOriginHidden; infer_instance

instance (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Decidable (ShapeOK n ls) := by
  unfold ShapeOK; infer_instance

theorem enterPre_shapeOK {s : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)}
    (h : EnterPreBase s ps ls) : ShapeOK s.P.length ls := h.2.2

/-- Static preconditions of `alloc provider owner shape` (B5; C6; D2): the allocator value at
`provider` is usable, with the right to update its metadata; the place `owner`, which receives
the ownership, is usable, with exercisable `Modify`; the leaves of the provider are `Init`; the
shape is well-formed and not empty (D2: an allocation of size zero is a shape of one leaf). -/
def AllocStatic (k : K) (s : S3) (provider owner : Nat)
    (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  s.Usable provider ∧ ProviderRight k s provider ∧ s.Usable owner ∧ HasRight s .modify owner ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P provider, s.I l = .init) ∧ ShapeOK s.P.length ls ∧ ls ≠ []

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (provider owner : Nat)
    (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Decidable (AllocStatic k s provider owner ls) := by
  unfold AllocStatic; infer_instance

/-- Places after `alloc` (B5; C6): the elements of the shape appended, those without owning
element owned by `owner`. -/
def allocP (s : S3) (owner : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Place :=
  shapeP s.P (.place owner) ls

/-- Effect of `alloc provider owner shape` (B5; C6): the elements of the shape appended as places
of fresh identities, `Uninit`, without anchor, alive, not freed, not pinned; one root authority
`Modify` per root element, on its footprint, held by the owner of the element (A4); the metadata
of the provider, its leaves, set to `Init`. The shape is abstract: it fixes neither alignment nor
layout (milestone 2). -/
def allocEff (s : S3) (provider owner : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : S3 :=
  { s with
    P := allocP s owner ls
    I := fun l => if s.P.length ≤ l then .uninit
      else if l ∈ footprint s.P provider then .init else s.I l
    A := s.A ++ (rootIdx ls).map fun i =>
      ⟨.modify, none, footprint (allocP s owner ls) (s.P.length + i),
        shapeOwner ls (.place owner) i, true⟩
    D := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then [] else s.D q
    dead := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.dead q
    freed := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.freed q
    pin := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then false else s.pin q }

/-- `alloc provider owner shape` as a relation (B5; C6; C9): `reject` when a static precondition
fails; `fail`, with the state unchanged, when the allocator contract cannot satisfy the request in
the current state (`Satisfiable`); `ok` otherwise. -/
inductive AllocStep (k : K) (provider owner : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat))
    (s : S3) : AOutcome → Prop where
  | ok : AllocStatic k s provider owner ls → k.Satisfiable provider ls s →
      AllocStep k provider owner ls s (.ok (allocEff s provider owner ls))
  | fail : AllocStatic k s provider owner ls → ¬ k.Satisfiable provider ls s →
      AllocStep k provider owner ls s (.fail s)
  | reject : ¬ AllocStatic k s provider owner ls → AllocStep k provider owner ls s .reject

/-- Determinism of `alloc` (B5). -/
theorem alloc_det {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)} {s : S3}
    {o₁ o₂ : AOutcome} (h₁ : AllocStep k pr ow ls s o₁) (h₂ : AllocStep k pr ow ls s o₂) :
    o₁ = o₂ := by
  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction

/-- `alloc_fail_unchanged` (B5; C9): a failed allocation leaves the state unchanged, and happens
exactly when the static preconditions hold and the allocator contract cannot satisfy the request
in the current state. -/
theorem alloc_fail_unchanged {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)}
    {s s' : S3} (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.fail s')) :
    s' = s ∧ AllocStatic k s pr ow ls ∧ ¬ k.Satisfiable pr ls s := by
  cases h with
  | fail h1 h2 => exact ⟨rfl, h1, h2⟩

section Shape
variable {P : List Place} {hd : Holder} {ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)}

theorem shapeP_len (P : List Place) (hd : Holder) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    (shapeP P hd ls).length = P.length + ls.length := by simp [shapeP]

theorem shapeP_lt {q : Nat} (h : q < P.length) : (shapeP P hd ls)[q]? = P[q]? :=
  List.getElem?_append_left h

theorem shapeP_new {i : Nat} (h : i < ls.length) : (shapeP P hd ls)[P.length + i]? =
    some ⟨(ls[i]?).bind (·.1), shapeOwner ls hd i, ((ls[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩ := by
  simp only [shapeP, List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_add_right _ _), Nat.add_sub_cancel_left,
    List.getElem?_map, List.getElem?_range h, Option.map_some]
